newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $64 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $64 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $64.00 per cwt in light volume near midday Wednesday, unchanged from active sales on Tuesday, feedlot sources said.
About 4,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the weekly movement near 133,000, including Friday's brisk trade, they said.
Sales in Kansas were pegged near 1,000 head, with a weekly movement near 133,500, the sources said.
Fed cattle prices were down $1.00 from thin sales Friday and off $2.00 from last week's top, with declines fueled by ample cattle supplies and weak beef prices, sources said.
Outlooks for expanding supplies of market-ready cattle into the summer as a result of active placements during the spring also weighed on prices, cattle feeders said.
However, the number of cattle sold this week, along with brisk beef sales on Tuesday and near midday Wednesday, generated perceptions beef demand was improving at the recent lower prices.
Beef prices at midday Wednesday were quoted down $0.45 to $0.67 per cwt on 258 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. Tuesday's sales totaled 391 loads.
Heavyweight choice beef at midday Wednesday was quoted at $102.52 per cwt, down $0.67 from Tuesday's close and down $1.00 from Friday.
